result.rootCause:
The speaking decision is a hard `viewing` gate written in two places, and neither has a "nobody is looking" branch.

1. `src/ImmersiveAI.Module/ImmersiveChatBehavior.cs:3683-3693` (`QuickChatRespondAsync`, the dispatcher lambda) is where EVERY window reply lands:
   `bool viewing = UI.TalkUI.IsViewing(npc);` … `if (viewing && Voice.VoiceService.AutoSpeakEnabled) Voice.VoiceService.Speak(npc, outcome.Reply);`
   The comment above it argues the rule deliberately: "Only when the player is actually reading this thread: a voice from a conversation they walked away from is a ghost in the room." That is the exact judgement Anton is now overturning for the closed case.

2. `ImmersiveChatBehavior.cs:1458-1463` (`GreetOnTalkScreenAsync`) repeats the same shape for the greeting that plays when a talk is opened from the vanilla dialog: `if (UI.TalkUI.IsViewing(npc) && AutoSpeakEnabled) Speak(...) else NotifyReplyReady(npc);`

So the handoff note's "find the reply-ready notice path, that is where the speaking belongs" resolves to the identical block; there is no separate closed-window path to hunt for.

result.risks:
WHAT COULD BREAK, and what standing law each edit stands nearest.

1. **The barge-in — same hazard as reach-outs, and strictly smaller.** `VoiceService.Speak` (269-331) increments `_generation` and calls `VoicePlayback.Begin`, which drops the queue and marks the current piece for release on the next tick. So a second answer CUTS OFF the first mid-sentence. The generation counter protects CORRECTNESS, not politeness: it guarantees no two voices overlap and that late audio for a passed moment is discarded (`Enqueue` 209-218, `SynthJob.Abandoned` 932-933, the pour's own re-check at 501-506) — it does not queue. So the exposure is real, and it is bounded by how many messages the player deliberately sent before closing: `_quickChatBusy` (3653) allows one in flight per soul, so two closed-window answers require the player to have messaged two souls and shut the screen. That is a smaller hazard than the reach-out case, which is unbidden and can fire for any co-located soul on any hourly tick — and Anton accepted THAT one on 2026.08.15 (`VoiceSpeakReachOuts = true`, ModConfig.cs:888-894). Hence: its own key, so it can be refused, but default ON.

2. **Why it needs its own key and cannot simply ride `VoiceAutoSpeak`.** `VoiceAutoSpeak` means "a reply speaks itself the moment it appears" (ModConfig.cs:814-816). Silently widening it to "and also when nothing appeared" would change what a shipped setting means for every player who already has it on — the small lie a setting never gets forgiven for, which is the exact argument written at ImmersiveChatBehavior.cs:1331-1335 about the panel. The new key rides UNDER it (helper returns early on `!AutoSpeakEnabled`), so one switch still silences everything.

3. **Money.** With a HOSTED voice cast, every walked-away-from reply now bills a TTS minute (`UsageLedger.NoteVoiceMinutes`, measured off the WAV header). The delta over today is only the replies the player did not read — today's `VoiceAutoSpeak = true` already bills every reply they DO read. Named in the MCM hint so it is never a surprise. The prewarm rule is untouched, so nothing is billed for audio nobody asked for.

4. **Standing laws touched: none, and that is deliberate.** No Core change → no prompt text, no beat marks, no first-person voice, no privacy fence, no numbers spoken in a refusal. Nothing is recorded to memory; nothing is written to a ledger. This is a garnish over a reply that has already landed and been recorded. The nearest law is the voice feature's own founding one — "NOTHING HERE MAY EVER COST A LINE" (VoiceService.cs:32-35) — honoured by the helper's total try/catch: every failure road ends in silence plus a log line, and the words are already safe in `memories.json` before this runs.

5. **The one behaviour delta to call out in review:** in `GreetOnTalkScreenAsync`, viewing + auto-speak OFF used to toast "has answered" at a player already reading the words. It now does not. That aligns it with the quick-chat road (3685) and is arguably the fix, but it IS a change and should not slip past unremarked.

6. **Ordering risk with the sibling planner.** Both this and the acted-parts item add a `Voices` MCM property and four `McmBridge` lines within ~10 lines of each other (255/291/358/466). Expect a textual conflict; both are additive and the merge is mechanical. Assign Order 6 here, Order 5 there.

7. **THE PANIC KEY ALREADY REACHES THIS CASE — confirmed from the code, no change needed.** `SubModule.OnApplicationTick` (104-126) calls `TickPanicKey()` (145-169) unconditionally, with no gate on the map, a campaign, a game state or a window — argued at 139-143 ("the whole value is that it works at the moment everything else has gone wrong"). Its only guard is `if (!Voice.VoicePlayback.IsSpeaking) return;`, and `IsSpeaking` (VoicePlayback.cs:162-166) is `_active || _current != null`, with `_active` set synchronously inside `Begin` (181-200) at the instant `Speak` is called — so Backspace works from before the first sample exists, through the whole reply, on the map, in a menu, or in a mission. `VoiceService.Stop()` then bumps the generation, which also abandons the still-running synthesis job. Nothing about a closed window changes any of that.

result.tests:
**none** for Core — and that is a fact about the change, not a gap. Nothing in `src/ImmersiveAI.Core` is touched: `Voices\SpeakableText`, `VoiceCacheKey`, `VoiceBudget`, `WavFiles`, `VoiceCasting` and `VoiceSeeds` are all untouched, so `netstandard2.0` gains no dependency and the existing suite is unaffected. Still run `dotnet test -c Release` after building, to prove exactly that.

The whole change is Module glue: one config bool, one private judgement method, two call sites rerouted, five MCM lines. That is the layer the project verifies by playtest, so what stands in for tests is a named checklist. Verify in this order, voices ON with a local voice cast on one soul (a hosted voice costs money to test and proves nothing extra — the road below the plan is shared):

1. **The ask itself.** Talk screen → message someone → close the screen → ride. Her answer speaks, and the "<Name> has answered." notice still fires beside it. (Both must happen: the toast is also the unread pointer back.)
2. **Nothing regressed while reading.** Same, screen left open on that soul: she speaks exactly as before, no toast.
3. **The other-thread rail.** Message Ava, switch to Sibylla, leave the screen open. Ava's answer must be SILENT — unread dot and toast only — and pressing ▶ on her line must speak it.
4. **The classic window shape.** Set `UseClassicChatWindow: true` and repeat 1-3. It must behave identically (one funnel, `SendQuickChat`); if it does not, something was edited in a VM instead of the behavior.
5. **The battle rail.** Message someone, close, get into a fight before the answer lands. Silence in the mission; the ▶ in the thread still plays it afterwards.
6. **The conversation rail.** Message A, close, start a vanilla conversation with B. A must not speak over B.
7. **The switch.** Turn "Speak answers that arrive while you are away" off in MCM mid-session (RequireRestart false) and repeat 1 — silence, no restart. Then turn "Speak without being asked" off with the new one still on — also silence, proving it rides underneath.
8. **The panic key.** Repeat 1 and press Backspace mid-sentence, on the map with every window shut. It must cut instantly. (Expected to pass untouched; it is on the checklist because it is the claim being made rather than a change being made.)
9. **The greeting road.** Approach someone on the map → "Speak freely" → close the screen while she is drawing breath. Her greeting speaks. This is the 1458-1463 edit's only real exercise.
10. **Log check** in `log.txt` for case 1: one `voice: making a line…` or `voice: … from the cache`, then `playing …` and `handed over …` lines. A `voice: a piece arrived for a moment that had passed` line here means the generation is being bumped by something after the speak, which would be a real bug.

Read by hand and verified; below is only what reading could NOT settle.

1. **Does `SoundEvent.CreateEventFromExternalFile(..., scene: null, ...)` actually play inside a mission?** `VoicePlayback.Create` (564-589) passes `scene: null`, and nothing in the file gates on a mission. I have gated speaking OUT of missions on judgement, not on measurement, so this is untested either way. If Anton later wants voices in a battle, the gate is one line to remove — but test it there, because a null-scene event in a mission scene is exactly the sort of thing that either works fine or returns a null sound event.

2. **Whether the mission rail is the judgement Anton wants at all.** "Doing something else" plainly covers riding, the map, inventory, the party screen — all allowed. A battle or a tavern scene is my call, on the grounds that a voice from an empty scene with nothing on screen to explain it gets reported as a bug. It is one line (`if (!IsSafeForLetterUi()) return;`) and it is the first thing to flip if he disagrees.

3. **Whether the other-thread rail (`UI.TalkUI.IsOpen`) matches his mental model.** He said "with the talk screen shut", which the rail honours literally. But a player who messages two souls and watches one page may well expect to hear both. Cheapest alternative if so: drop the `IsOpen` check and let `viewing || VoiceSpeakWhenClosed` decide — one line, and it raises the barge-in exposure to what reach-outs already carry.

4. **The hearth window (H) is not in `TalkUI.IsOpen`** (UI/TalkUI.cs:50-53 counts the talk screen and the two classic windows only). So a reply landing while the H window is open WILL speak. I judged that right — the hearth is a different room, like the map — but it is an untested consequence of reusing an existing predicate, not a decision anyone made.

5. **Time compression.** With the screen shut the clock runs, possibly fast. A 15-second reply may speak across two in-game days, and `_endsUtc` is wall-clock so playback itself is unaffected. Whether anything ELSE misbehaves when a voice spans a day boundary (an hourly tick firing a reach-out that barges in, say) is unproven. Watch for it in playtest step 1 at high speed.

6. **A voice already in the air when a mission starts keeps playing into it.** Confirmed by reading (nothing stops it), NOT confirmed by ear. This gap exists today for reach-outs, so it is pre-existing rather than introduced — which is why the `OnMissionBehaviorInitialize` fix is listed as optional and separate.

7. **Whether the hosted road's latency without prewarm is actually tolerable.** I argued from the code (single-flight means prewarming saves latency, never money) that the rule should stand, but nobody has heard a hosted voice start cold on a closed-window reply. If it feels slow, the honest fix is NOT to make `Prewarm` eager for remote voices — it is to hoist the "will this be spoken" decision, and the `Describe` DO-NOT-WIDEN warning (VoiceService.cs:415-440) says how not to do that. Re-open the question with a measurement, not a guess.

8. **`VoiceSpeakReachOuts` in CLAUDE.md was already wrong** (line 1773 says "off"; the code says `true` since 2026.08.15). I have folded the correction into this change's doc edit. If some other doc or store page repeats the "off" claim, I did not find it — grep across CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, README.md and the two voiceover docs returned that single hit.

DeclineTheFeast and WithholdTheName have no other callers (verified by grep). FAILURE, two ways in. (a) Pre-update record: the player's wife bore him a child before this batch and the offer is still inside its 30-day window; he rides in, correctly gets the ordinary feast popup, has no spare gold and clicks "No feast" - `Owned = Withheld`, a permanent PlayerEngaged MotherNameBeat into her memory ("Mizam has not owned Ira before anyone... none of that is the same as his having said so", lines 693-696), AwaitsTheName true, the child into ChildrenAwaitingTheName()/UnnamedChildrenOf(), and HouseLine's `unsaid` bucket forever ("Sibylla is raising a child he has never owned before anyone"). (b) No migration involved: a child born to a lover whom the player then MARRIES before the offer fires - mustOwnIt is false so the popup deliberately does not raise the question, and "No feast" answers it anyway as "say nothing".
findings.fix: Smallest local fix: carry the popup's own verdict into the callback. Change `_ => DeclineTheFeast(record)` (Births.cs:617) to `_ => DeclineTheFeast(record, mustOwnIt)` - mustOwnIt is already a local and closes over cleanly - and make it `private void DeclineTheFeast(BirthRecord record, bool wasAskedAboutOwning)` (line 833) calling WithholdTheName only when wasAskedAboutOwning, so one test never answers another. If the CircumstanceKnown field from the finding above is taken, also tighten WithholdTheName's own guard to `if (record == null || !record.BornOutsideMarriage) return;` so no future caller can reach the recorder with the wrong idea.

findings.title: A bought feast records a QUIET owning, and records one for children of the marriage who were never in question
findings.evidence: NOT IN THE LEADS. Line 606: `if (pick is BirthScale scale) { OwnTheChild(record, late: false); HoldTheFeast(record, scale); }`, and the signature is `OwnTheChild(BirthRecord record, bool late, bool withFeast = false)` (line 638), so withFeast is left false and reaches MotherNameBeat at line 660. BirthText.MotherNameBeat's withFeast:true branch ("owned {childNames} before a hall full of people and gave the child his name", BirthText.cs:233) is therefore DEAD in production - a grep for `withFeast` finds it passed true nowhere outside the tests. Every feast-bought owning instead writes the false branch: "Mizam owned Ira - quietly, with no hall and no herald, but he said it, and it was heard." Beat marks are permanent and never reworded (BirthText's own NameMark rule). Second half of the same line: OwnTheChild runs for EVERY feast pick, including a child of the marriage where mustOwnIt was false and the popup never mentioned owning - so buying a feast for a legitimate child sets Owned = Given, fires "[cradle] Ira is yours before the world." (line 675), and writes the mother a PlayerEngaged recognition beat plus each child a ChildNameBeat. The design's rule is the opposite: "A child of a marriage is his by the fact of the marriage and is never asked about" (BirthRecord.cs:22-23, and the design record's Recognition section). Ordering compounds it: OwnTheChild runs BEFORE HoldTheFeast, which re-runs the purse and can bail out (lines 951-956), leaving "owned" recorded for a feast never kept. FAILURE: player wed to Sibylla buys the 500,000-denar feast for their son; her memory permanently holds "Mizam owned Ira - quietly, with no hall and no herald" about the largest hall in Calradia, for a child nobody ever questioned, and the notice tells the player his wife's son "is yours before the world" - the whole vocabulary of bastard recognition dropped into a marriage the design says it must never enter. The same wording lands on the case the branch was written for: a lover's child feasted in public still remembers the day as a quiet word with no herald.
findings.fix: In the chosen-callback at Births.cs:606, gate the owning on the popup's own verdict and tell the truth about the hall: `if (pick is BirthScale scale) { HoldTheFeast(record, scale); if (mustOwnIt && record.Scale != BirthScale.Unfeasted) OwnTheChild(record, late: false, withFeast: true); }` - HoldTheFeast first so a purse emptied since the choosing cannot record a hall that was never kept (it sets record.Scale only on success), and mustOwnIt so a child of the marriage keeps the plain feast it always had. Leave line 607 (QuietOwning) exactly as it is; it is the withFeast:false case and is already correct.

findings.title: A female player with a pre-update child is asked whether her own child is hers, and told she is not her own wife
findings.evidence: NOT IN THE LEADS - a facet of the migration bug on a path the self-review's live check cannot see. `bool mustOwnIt = !record.BornInMarriage && !Safe(() => FamilyBuilder.AreWed(Hero.MainHero, mother), false);` with `var mother = record.MotherIsPlayer ? Hero.MainHero : ...` at line 526. FamilyBuilder.AreWed opens `if (a == null || b == null || a == b) return false;` (FamilyBuilder.cs:194), so when the player IS the mother the live-wed rescue is structurally false and mustOwnIt collapses to `!record.BornInMarriage`, true for every pre-update record. The popup then uses the ownership title ("Is this child yours before the world?", line 591), skips the purse gate (line 548), and prints `record.MotherName + " is not your wife."` (line 581) using the player's OWN name; "Say nothing" then reaches WithholdTheName (see the finding above) and marks her own legitimate child Withheld. New records are safe: for a married female player BornInMarriage is computed true at capture (line 179). FAILURE: an existing campaign with a female player and children chronicled before this batch - a deferred offer fires inside the window and asks Ira (the player) "Is this child yours before the world?" over the body text "Ira is not your wife."
findings.fix: Add the player-as-mother case to the same guard at Births.cs:541: `bool mustOwnIt = !record.BornInMarriage && !record.MotherIsPlayer && !Safe(() => FamilyBuilder.AreWed(Hero.MainHero, mother), false);`. The recognition layer is written for a father owning a child before the world (HouseLine says "he has owned", OwnTheChild reads record.FatherName), so never raising the question when the player is the mother is both the smallest and the honest answer, and consistent with the design's "a female player is only kept from crashing". The CircumstanceKnown field removes the pre-update half independently; this line still wants the MotherIsPlayer clause.

findings.title: When the hour's account never arrives, the child's own beginning beat is never written at all
findings.evidence: NOT IN THE LEADS. RecordChildsOwnBeginning is called from exactly one place, RecordHourBeats (line 455), which returns early on `if (record.BirthBeatDone || string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(record.BirthAccount)) return;` (line 416). SweepBirthsThatNeverGotTheirBeat is the fallback for a birth whose chronicler failed all three attempts (lines 1267-1292): it hand-writes MotherHourBeat with "I have not set the hour itself down, but I carry it" and FatherBeat, then sets `record.BirthBeatDone = true` - and never calls RecordChildsOwnBeginning. So the one beat in the feature that costs nothing (ChildBornBeat is hand-written: "no LLM, and this costs one hand-written line", BirthText.cs:241) is the only one lost when a paid call fails. The sweep's own sibling fix already carries the argument: "His mark never depended on the chronicler at all, so losing it here was pure oversight" (lines 1281-1282) - as true of the child as of the father. FAILURE: a child is born while the key is rate-limited and all three hour attempts fail; the mother gets her hand-written mark, the father gets his, and the newborn's memory file stays empty. Eighteen years later it comes of age and first speaks knowing nothing of its own beginning - no birth, no place, no mother, and for a lover's child no record of the silence it was born into, which is the single memory the child's-own-story feature exists to create.
findings.fix: In SweepBirthsThatNeverGotTheirBeat (Births.cs), add `RecordChildsOwnBeginning(record);` immediately before `record.BirthBeatDone = true;` at line 1291 - the same one-line repair the father's mark already got two blocks above. The child's beat needs no account to be written, so nothing else moves.

findings.title: A feast/owning offer that lapses is read as 'he owned the child' - the decision, with the migration danger weighed
findings.evidence: `IsOwnedBeforeTheWorld => Owned != Acknowledgement.Withheld` and `AwaitsTheName => Owned == Acknowledgement.Withheld && AnyLived`. Nothing settles the record when the window closes: WithholdTheName is called only from DeclineTheFeast (line 840), and AwaitingFeastOffer simply stops yielding past FeastOfferDays (BirthLedger.cs:185-189). FeastSideSettled (lines 851-857) treats the lapse as settled for SEALING and deliberately does not touch Owned. So a lapsed out-of-marriage child reads owned - HouseLine puts it in the `owned` bucket, "he has owned before the world as his, by Ira", a public claim never made - while AwaitsTheName stays false, which closes the late giving of the name permanently: GiveTheNameTo requires AwaitsTheName (line 715) and refuses with "is not waiting on a name from you", ChildrenAwaitingTheNameBy returns empty so the Between-us page's ActionLabel "Give <child> your name" never appears (Courtship.cs:1709-1748), and UnnamedChildrenOf returns 0 so the lover's craving - the concrete object her whole arc is built on - never engages. FAILURE: the player fathers a child on his lover while campaigning and never rides back inside thirty days (TryOfferTheFeast requires IsCoLocated(mother), line 528). The window closes with Owned = NeverArose; every wife's and lover's sheet says he owned the child before the world, the player is never told he decided anything, and the heavy act the recognition road exists for is unreachable for that child forever.
findings.fix: RECOMMENDATION: settle a lapsed window to Withheld - but ONLY after the CircumstanceKnown/BornOutsideMarriage field from the first finding lands, and gated on it. WHY SETTLE: (1) NeverArose currently means two contradictory things at once and the house line reads the wrong one aloud on every reply; (2) the design's own reading of silence is withholding - "Say nothing and the child is still yours by blood, and grows up in its mother's shadow" (the popup body, Births.cs:584) - and a month of not riding home IS saying nothing; (3) Withheld is REVERSIBLE at any age via GiveTheNameTo, while an accidental Given is a permanent fiction stated on every sheet, and that asymmetry decides it. THE MIGRATION DANGER, which is the whole reason to gate: a settler testing only `!BornInMarriage && Owned == NeverArose && today - GameDay > FeastOfferDays && !FeastOffered` would, on the first hourly tick after the update, mark EVERY existing child in EVERY existing campaign Withheld - precisely the catastrophe RecognitionTests.AnOldRecordIsNeverQuietlyDisowned guards and the design record calls "the safety that matters most". With BornOutsideMarriage (false on every record written before the field) the settler is safe by construction. SHAPE: one pass in TendTheBirthChronicle beside OfferPendingFeasts - `foreach (var record in _birthLedger.Records.ToList()) if (record.BornOutsideMarriage && record.Owned == Acknowledgement.NeverArose && record.AnyLived && today - record.GameDay > BirthLedger.FeastOfferDays) WithholdTheName(record);` - snapshotting the list, per the 2026.08.10 mutation lesson at line 1252. ONE REFINEMENT: on this path WithholdTheName's beat should ride OutreachMark.None rather than PlayerEngaged, because nothing happened in the room - she is noticing a month of silence, not being answered to her face.

findings.title: HouseLine's group-separator test compares freshly built IGrouping instances, so it is always true
findings.evidence: NOT IN THE LEADS; cosmetic only. `if (byWife.Count > 0 || group != owned.GroupBy(c => c.MotherName ?? string.Empty).First()) sb.Append(' ');` re-runs GroupBy inside the loop, and GroupBy is lazy - each enumeration constructs new Grouping objects - so `group`, which came from the foreach's own enumeration, is never reference-equal to the freshly built First(), and the guard never suppresses anything. Line 174 has already left a trailing space after "...as the world may speak of it: ", so with no children of the marriage the first owned group gets a second one. The `unsaid` loop at line 190 appends ' ' unconditionally and has the same seam when both earlier buckets are empty. FAILURE: a player with only out-of-marriage children gets "Of Mizam's house, as the world may speak of it:  Tulag he has owned before the world as his, by Ira." - a double space mid-line. Harmless to meaning, but it is prompt text riding every reply of every woman of the hearth.
findings.fix: In BirthText.HouseLine, collect the three sentences into a `List<string>` and emit `header + string.Join(" ", parts)` instead of appending separators by hand; that removes the reference comparison entirely and nothing else in the method changes.

findings.title: A pending pre-update feast offer asks the ownership question
findings.evidence: Fixed 2026.08.15 with the comment at lines 536-542: "THE CHOICE IS THREE-WAY FOR A CHILD BORN OUTSIDE A MARRIAGE (2026.08.15) - and the question is asked of the LIVE world, not only of the record: every birth written before this field existed carries BornInMarriage = false, and asking a long-married player whether his wife's child is his would be absurd (self-review). If she is his wife today, no such question arises." The code now reads `bool mustOwnIt = !record.BornInMarriage && !Safe(() => FamilyBuilder.AreWed(Hero.MainHero, mother), false);`, so the title, the QuietOwning element, the "<mother> is not your wife" paragraph and the decline label all fall back to the ordinary feast popup for a wife. NOTE this covers only the FIRST clause of the lead; the second clause ("and can mark a legitimate child Withheld") survives untouched and is reported above as REAL at line 685, and the player-as-mother path escapes this guard entirely, reported above at line 541.

findings.title: The free 'Own the child' choice is hidden behind a gold check meant only for feasts
findings.evidence: The purse gate now carries the mustOwnIt exemption at lines 544-548: "An empty purse is not a question - EXCEPT when one of the answers is free. Owning a child quietly costs nothing and is the whole point of the choice; gating it behind the cheapest feast meant a broke man could never say the child was his (self-review, 2026.08.15)." The code is `if (!mustOwnIt && (Hero.MainHero?.Gold ?? 0) < BirthTiers.All.Min(t => t.Price)) return false;`. A penniless player fathering a child outside a marriage now always gets the three-way popup, so Acknowledgement.Given and Withheld are both reachable and UnnamedChildrenOf engages. The duplicate lead at the same site ("suppressed by a purse check meant for feasts", ChildrenAwaitingTheName never populated) is the same defect and the same fix.

findings.title: The child's own first beat asserts recognition before the player has been asked
findings.evidence: RecordChildsOwnBeginning now passes `record.BornInMarriage`, not IsOwnedBeforeTheWorld, with the fix argued at lines 473-479: "owned: only what is CERTAIN at this instant. This runs when the hour's account arrives, which is BEFORE the player has answered the owning question - and IsOwnedBeforeTheWorld reads 'yes' while it is still unasked, so using it here made every child's own first memory assert a recognition that had not happened yet (self-review, 2026.08.15). A child of the marriage is the only one certainly owned now; the rest get their line from OwnTheChild when the answer actually comes." An out-of-marriage newborn therefore gets ChildBornBeat's silent branch ("Nothing was said of it before anyone", BirthText.cs:254) and, if the player later owns it, an appended ChildNameBeat from OwnTheChild (line 670). The duplicate lead at line 476 is the same defect. This path only ever reads a FRESHLY captured record, so the pre-update migration hole does not reach it.

findings.title: PlayerHouseLine is written in the player's first person and folded into the NPC's own first-person sheet
findings.evidence: Touches Core/Births, so reported here for completeness. HouseLine now takes `string hisName` and writes the whole line in the third person - "Of " + him + "'s house, as the world may speak of it: ... born of his marriage ... he has owned before the world as his ... he has never owned before anyone ... he has said nothing of it." - with the reason on the parameter itself (lines 158-161): "IT IS NOT THE READER - this line rides the sheet of the women of his household, where 'I' means HER. Written in his own first person it made every wife and lover claim his children as her own, which is exactly the kind of quiet voice break this mod exists not to make (self-review, 2026.08.15)." RecognitionTests.AWithheldChildAppearsOnlyInHerLine pins it: `Assert.Contains("Of Mizam's house", line); Assert.DoesNotContain("I have owned", line); Assert.DoesNotContain("my marriage", line);` (RecognitionTests.cs:78-83). The remaining defect on this line is WHICH BUCKET each child lands in, reported as REAL at Births.cs:751.

result.notes:
SHAPE OF THE AREA. Three of the five leads I was given are genuinely fixed (the gold gate, the child's premature recognition beat, the ownership question put to a married player) and the fix comments are all stamped and quotable. What survives is ONE root cause wearing four coats: BirthRecord.BornInMarriage is a two-state bool standing in for a three-state fact, and `false` means both "known outside a marriage" and "written before we asked". The Acknowledgement enum next to it solved that exact problem by making NeverArose = 0; the bool never got the same treatment. The 2026.08.15 self-review patched the ONE read that hurt loudest (the popup) with a live-world check and left the other three reads - HouseOfThePlayerLine's two and WithholdTheName's guard - on the raw bool. Fix the field and four findings collapse into one small change; patch the sites one at a time and the next reader finds the fifth.

WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT REPORT. (1) The chronicler is never told whether the parents were wed - Facts carries only MarriedPhrase, simply absent for a lover - so a lover's birth account is written in the same register as a marriage's. That is consistent with the locked decision "Bastard children draw no world commentary yet" and is prompt tuning, not a defect; it belongs to the playtest, not the fixer. (2) FullAccount/RollEntry/ChronicleEntry say nothing about recognition; the public state deliberately lives in the house line. (3) ForgeBirthChronicleFor re-runs RecordChildsOwnBeginning on an existing record and would write a second beginning beat - dev lever, and re-forging is what it is for. (4) HouseLine's "he" for a female player: the whole recognition/nights layer is male-player by Anton's explicit call, and PlayerHouseLine only rides sheets of souls with a bond kind, so I judged it out of scope rather than broken.

ORDER TO APPLY. The CircumstanceKnown/BornOutsideMarriage field first (it is the root, and it is what makes the lapse decision safe); then the DeclineTheFeast signature; then the feast-owning call at line 606; then the sweep's missing child beat; the lapse settler LAST, since it is the only one that touches existing campaigns' data. Every one of them wants `dotnet test` - RecognitionTests is where these guarantees live and it should grow one case per change.

result.area: Doors with reasons, and the duty night — src/ImmersiveAI.Module/ImmersiveChatBehavior.Doors.cs, src/ImmersiveAI.Core/Doors/, and the duty-night half of ImmersiveChatBehavior.Nights.cs

findings.title: The duty-night spiral saturates: a 4-card deck laid by Restates-refusal against a cap of 5, and the refusal is discarded
findings.evidence: LayDutyNightReason is the WHOLE of the spiral: `var card = DoorText.DrawDutyReason(seed); if (!DoorReasons.SetDown(memory.DoorReasons, card.Text, card.Opens, CampaignTime.Now.ToDays, out _, byTheWorld: true)) return;   // already as deep as this mechanism goes; piling on is only noise`. DoorText.DutyNightReasons (DoorText.cs:114-136) holds EXACTLY 4 cards. SetDown (DoorReasons.cs:95-104) refuses on `Text.LooseMatch.Restates(Standing(reasons)...)` — and the four card texts share no containment, so all four can stand at once — and refuses again at `OpenCount(reasons) >= MaxStandingOpen` (=5, DoorReasons.cs:44). FAILURE: the closure provably stops deepening. Once the drawn card already stands (~8 duty nights by coupon-collector, sooner if any of her own reasons occupy slots), and unconditionally once 5 things stand, every further duty night lays NOTHING: nothing new appears on the Between-us page, DoorText.Page's own tally ("Of these, N were not raised in any conversation. They are nights.", DoorText.cs:237-242) freezes at 4 while the player spends thirty duty nights, and the road back stops lengthening — the night is free from then on. The design guardrail is unconditional: "The spiral must bite: a duty night that costs nothing breaks the whole moral of the design. If playtests show it farmable, deepen the closure, do not soften the door." The section itself offers the missing half: "a new written reason of hers, OR THE STANDING ONE GROWS HARDER (implementation's choice, but it must be visible in her words on the Between-us page)". Only the first half is built. I judge this a real gap rather than tuning: the card count and the cap ARE tuning, but 'nothing at all happens' is the failure the guardrail names by name, and the design's own second mechanism is simply absent.
findings.fix: Build the design's other half in the existing shape, without touching MaxStandingOpen or the deck size. (1) Core/Doors/DoorReason.cs: add `public int TimesRepeated { get; set; }` beside LaidByTheWorld (old JSON loads 0). (2) Core/Doors/DoorReasons.cs: add `public static bool DeepenByTheWorld(List<DoorReason> reasons, string cardText, double day)` — find the standing reason that LooseMatch.Restates the drawn card, else the oldest STANDING reason with LaidByTheWorld true; if none exists return false (5 of her own words already standing IS maximum closure, and bumping her own line would be the mod writing on her list); otherwise `found.TimesRepeated++; found.SetDownDay = day;` and return true. (3) Module/ImmersiveChatBehavior.Doors.cs LayDutyNightReason: on the SetDown refusal call DeepenByTheWorld before returning, and SaveMemory when it took. (4) Core/Doors/DoorText.cs: render the count where it is already read — Section() after "(this still stands)" and Page() after the bullet, as "and it has happened N times since" (silent below 2). Each duty night then stays visible in her own words and on the Between-us page forever, and the mending lengthens by informing HER — settling stays her judgment alone, nothing is gated. Extend DoorTests.ADutyNightLaysSomethingDownWhetherOrNotSheIsInATalk with ten successive draws asserting something moves on every one.

findings.title: LayDutyNightReason writes her memory with no in-flight guard — and its SaveMemory consumes the duty beat that was just parked for safety
findings.evidence: NOT IN THE LEADS (they named this shape only for LeakTheBond/MarkFreshWound, outside my area; this instance is inside it and is strictly worse). GoToHerAnyway (Nights.cs:815-820) does `WriteNightBeat(wife, NightText.DutyBeat(...))` — which correctly parks into _pendingWeddingBeats when `IsExchangeInFlight(wife)` (Nights.cs:1607-1613) — then immediately `LayDutyNightReason(wife, record.Id)`, which does a bare `LoadMemory(wife)` / `SaveMemory(wife, memory)` with no such guard. SaveMemory (ImmersiveChatBehavior.cs:834-840) calls FoldPendingWeddingBeats, whose body is `if (!_pendingWeddingBeats.TryRemove(npc.StringId, out var beats) ...) return;` (Weddings.cs:69) — a REMOVE. FAILURE: player sends a line to his wife in the classic chat window (time runs on the map, unlike the talk screen); her reply is still in flight when hour 21 ticks and the evening's notice goes up; he clicks it and picks "<name> — go to her anyway". WriteNightBeat parks the DutyBeat; LayDutyNightReason then loads her file from disk, sets down the card, and saves — folding AND REMOVING the parked beat into an instance the in-flight exchange is about to overwrite. Her reply lands and ExecutePlayerTurnAsync saves its stale liveMemory over the file. The DoorReason and the duty beat are both gone, the pending dictionary is empty so FlushParkedWeddingBeats has nothing to restore, and the duty night has cost literally nothing — no spiral, no memory of it — while the player was told "The duty of the marriage was kept." The contrast sits inside one method: the beat five lines above is guarded, the reason is not.
findings.fix: Register a fourth pending kind, exactly as _pendingBlessingFolds already does for a non-beat mutation (Courtship.cs:70-88 — note it uses TryGetValue, not TryRemove, so the fold is idempotent across repeated writes). In ImmersiveChatBehavior.Doors.cs add `private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<string, DoorReason> _pendingDoorReasons` and `private static void FoldPendingDoorReasons(Hero npc, NpcMemory memory)` that TryGetValues the card and calls DoorReasons.SetDown on the instance being written (SetDown's own Restates check makes the fold idempotent); call it from SaveMemory beside the other three folds (ImmersiveChatBehavior.cs:836-838); and in LayDutyNightReason park instead of writing when IsExchangeInFlight(wife). Clear the entry on the hourly sweep beside FlushParkedWeddingBeats. Reordering the two calls in GoToHerAnyway alone is NOT enough — it saves the beat but the stale instance still clobbers the reason.

findings.title: DoorReasons.Revise still accepts a revise that changes nothing and reports success — the guard its own doc-comment claims
findings.evidence: NOT IN THE LEADS — it is the residue of the 2026.08.16 fix for them. The method's remark states: "It also refuses a revise that would change NOTHING, for the same reason the misgivings' own revise never blanks: 'I have reworded it' over an untouched line is that same lie wearing a politer face." The implementation refuses only when BOTH new strings are empty: `if (body.Length == 0 && road.Length == 0) { trouble = "no new words were given for it"; return false; }`, then `if (body.Length > 0) found.Text = body;` with no comparison against found.Text. DoorTests.AReviseTakesTwoStrings_AndRefusesToRewriteAThingToItself only exercises the empty case (line 125), so the claim is untested as well as unimplemented. FAILURE: a model that fills `matter` and `reworded` with the same sentence (the schema discourages it, but nothing stops it, and HandsCameSwapped will not fire because Find(matter) succeeds) reproduces the exact 2026.08.16 bug — Find locates the reason, found.Text is set to the string it just matched on, Revise returns true, the resolver spends the turn's single deed (door.Acted = true), fires the frost/rose notice, and answers "I have reworded it. The shape of it changed…": the silent lie about what she just decided that DoorReasons.cs:156-160 says this system cannot afford.
findings.fix: In DoorReasons.Revise, after Find succeeds and before the assignments, add the no-op test the comment already promises: if `body` is empty-or-equal to Tidy(found.Text) AND `road` is empty-or-equal to Tidy(found.Opens) (ordinal, case-insensitive), set `trouble = "it already says exactly that"` and return false. Three lines, no signature change; the resolver's existing `if (!ok) return "It does not go down that way — {trouble}…"` then speaks the refusal out loud and the loop has rounds left to correct itself. Extend the existing test with `Assert.False(DoorReasons.Revise(reasons, x, x, "", out _))`.

findings.title: "Go to her anyway" checks presence, captivity, reachability and the cooldown
findings.evidence: All three duplicate leads (Doors.cs:115 twice, Nights.cs:466) describe code that no longer exists. CanGoToHerAnyway now carries, with the stamp: "// EVERYTHING THAT IS NOT THE DOOR STILL BINDS… Offering it anyway put 'go to her anyway' beside an absent wife, and let one be spent twice in an evening (self-review, 2026.08.15)." followed by `if (PresenceBlockFor(npc, out _).Length > 0) return false;`. PresenceBlockFor (Nights.cs:231-249) covers every item on the list: `if (wife == null || !wife.IsAlive) return "she is beyond your reach";` (dead), `if (wife.IsPrisoner) return "she is held captive";` (prisoner), `if (!IsCoLocated(wife)) return "she is not with you";` (not co-located), `if (settlement != null && IsBehindClosedDoors(wife, settlement)) return "you cannot reach her here";` (behind the keep's doors), and `double cooldown = CooldownHoursLeft(); if (cooldown > 0) …` (the night cooldown, counted hearth-wide from LastTogetherWithAnyone, which NightLedger.cs:184-186 explicitly makes count Duty nights: "A duty night counts here and nowhere else it is not wanted: it was still a night, and the clock does not care what it was"). The gate is honoured at all three sites the leads named: HandleTheEvening's `else if (CanGoToHerAnyway(wife)) shutAgainstYou.Add(wife);` (Nights.cs:298), AskWhereYouWillSleep's `if (block.Length > 0 && CanGoToHerAnyway(wife))` (Nights.cs:477), and GoToHerAnyway's re-check at the act (Nights.cs:790), whose comment now reads "CanGoToHerAnyway now carries the presence and cooldown checks too." A distant, captive, unreachable or cooling-off wife is therefore in neither shutAgainstYou nor the popup, so the enabled duty element and the conception-across-Calradia scenario are both unreachable.

findings.title: weigh_what_stands 'revise' takes two separate strings

findings.title: The lover road runs no kinship check at all — the player's own sister can become his lover and bear his child
findings.evidence: LoverWorldBlock (Lovers.cs:118-135) is the ONLY world-law leg on this road, and it reads in full: Gone / NotTheCustom (sex) / `if (npc.Spouse != null) return TrothBlock.NotFree;` / TooYoung / notable-minor-template / `if (!npc.IsWanderer && !npc.IsLord) return TrothBlock.NotForMarriage;`. No blood test of any kind. Its own doc-comment claims only THREE legs of the marriage road are dropped ("the player's own standing marriage, the station gate, and the companion-marriage setting") — kinship is a silently dropped fourth. I chased every other door: (1) LoverFactsOf (Lovers.cs:146) sets `WorldRefusesThePair = LoverWorldBlock(npc) != TrothBlock.None`, so LoverRoad.JudgeTake inherits exactly that and nothing more; (2) CanOfferSelf (Lovers.cs:54-74) adds only co-location + `known.CourtshipStage >= LoverRoad.ForksFrom` + JudgeTake; (3) OnLoverSealed (Lovers.cs:388) re-runs the same JudgeTake; (4) the dev lever MakeLoverFor (Lovers.cs:865) calls LoverWorldBlock and nothing else. The trunk that feeds the fork is no help: CanTendTroth (Courtship.cs:113) calls `TrothBlockReason(npc, forWedding: false, _config, forHand: false)` and TendCourtship steps with `forWedding: target == CourtshipStage.Wed` (Courtship.cs:528), while the game's own verdict is nested inside `if (forWedding) { ... if (!wanderer) { ... IsCoupleSuitableForMarriage ... } }` (Courtship.cs:233-251) — so IsCoupleSuitableForMarriage runs at exactly one place in the whole mod, the WEDDING lay, which the lover road never reaches. Nothing in FamilyBuilder bars kin either: it owns AreWed/SpousesOf and kinship WORDS ("my kinswoman"), no gate. FAILURE PATH, end to end: the player's unmarried adult sister (IsLord, Clan == PlayerClan, Spouse == null, 18+) walks the shared trunk to Devotion via tend_courtship (no kin leg on any step), reaches relation 70, offer_myself rides because CanOfferSelf passes, ShowLoverInquiry → OnLoverSealed seals the bond (Courtship.cs:1092 wires the seal), IsOfPlayerHousehold is true so BringHerAlong puts her in the party with no ransom (Lovers.cs:597-607), WomenOfTheHearth then lists her at dusk (Nights.cs:108-122), and RollForAChild → BorrowTheFatherSlot → MakePregnantAction.Apply (Nights.cs:1055-1057) fathers a child on her. I decompiled the live DLL to confirm the model is the real kinship authority: DefaultMarriageModel.IsCoupleSuitableForMarriage ANDs in `AreHeroesRelated(firstHero, secondHero, 3)`, and that method is PRIVATE, so it cannot be borrowed directly.
findings.fix: src/ImmersiveAI.Module/ImmersiveChatBehavior.Lovers.cs, method LoverWorldBlock — add one leg beside the existing `npc.Spouse != null` line: `if (FamilyBuilder.AreBloodKin(player, npc)) return TrothBlock.WorldRefuses;`. That single line closes every door at once, because LoverWorldBlock is read by JudgeTake at the LAY (CanOfferSelf / ResolveOfferSelf), at the SEAL (OnLoverSealed) and by the dev lever — the strike_bargain discipline already in place. Both wordings already exist and need no new text: her side is LoverText.TakeRefusal(WorldRefuses) ("The world would not have the two of us at all, whatever name we gave it", LoverText.cs:177-178) and the player's line is TakeRefusalForPlayer's default ("the world does not allow it as things stand"); TrothBlockForNpc(WorldRefuses) already names kinship outright. The helper goes in src/ImmersiveAI.Module/Personas/FamilyBuilder.cs beside AreWed: `public static bool AreBloodKin(Hero a, Hero b, int depth = 3)` — collect a's ancestors within `depth` generations via Hero.Father/Hero.Mother (a itself included) into a HashSet, do the same for b, return true on any intersection, all inside the file's own Safe/Try so a ragged family graph never throws. That is an exact behavioural mirror of vanilla's private AreHeroesRelated(a,b,3), so the lover road refuses precisely the pairs the wedding road already refuses at the altar (parent, child, sibling, grandparent, aunt/uncle, niece/nephew, first and second cousins). DO NOT reach for MarriageModel.IsCoupleSuitableForMarriage here: decompiled today it also ANDs in IsSuitableForMarriage (requires `IsLord`, so EVERY wanderer fails), IsClanSuitableForMarriage (false for a null clan, so an unhired wanderer fails), and a both-are-clan-leaders veto — i.e. it would re-impose exactly the station-and-house legs the design record drops on purpose. A blood-only leg bars blood without touching station, which is what the design asks for.

findings.title: LoverStandingLine still reads the cushioned band, so the player is told a sealed lover "stands at fondness" while she despises him
findings.evidence: Lovers.cs:816-817 still reads `return LoverText.StandingLine(memory.LoverBond, HeartBands.Of(GetStanding(npc), memory.CourtshipStage));` — the CUSHIONED reading. The 2026.08.15 self-review fixed the sibling call site (ImmersiveChatBehavior.Doors.cs:100-102) and left this one behind. HeartBands.Of drops the cushion only at `if (stage >= CourtshipStage.Betrothed) return band;` (HeartBands.cs:87), and a lover's stage never gets there: LoverRoad.JudgeTake refuses `f.Stage >= CourtshipStage.Betrothed` with PromiseStands (LoverRoad.cs:108), OnLoverSealed writes only memory.LoverBond and never the stage (Lovers.cs:398-400), and MakeLoverFor pins it at `LoverRoad.ForksFrom` = Devotion (Lovers.cs:874-877). So HeartBands.Of(-100, Devotion) returns Like and LoverText.StandingLine emits "yours, with nothing holding it but the heart — which stands at fondness" (LoverText.cs:291) about a woman at -100. It is not a hidden string: BondStatsLabel appends it to the bond line in both windows (ImmersiveChatBehavior.cs:2074-2075, over the comment "the line is the only place outside her own words that says so"), and RoadPageFor prints it as the Between-us page's "Where you stand: …" (ImmersiveChatBehavior.Courtship.cs:1694-1697). OPTIONAL hardening that makes the mistake unrepeatable and makes HeartBands' own remark true: give Core `HeartBands.Of` a `BondKind bond = BondKind.None` parameter and return `OfRelation(relation)` whenever `bond != BondKind.None` — LoverRoad.JudgeTake keeps the default (she is not yet anyone's, so the walking-the-road cushion is correct there) and both module call sites pass the real bond.

findings.title: The ransom seal writes the paid truth into the kinswoman's memory with no in-flight parking — the blessing seal, its own template, parks it
findings.evidence: NOT IN THE LEADS — found while reading around them. OnRansomSealed takes the gold (`GiveGoldAction.ApplyBetweenCharacters(player, npc, bless.Price);`, Lovers.cs:494) and then writes the bought truth into a THIRD party — the kinswoman, who is not the soul in the exchange — with a raw load/save: `var memory = LoadMemory(kin!); memory.LoverRansomPaid = bless.Price; AddSilentInnerBeat(...); SaveMemory(kin!, memory);` (Lovers.cs:496-500). LoadMemory re-reads memories.json from disk on every call (ImmersiveChatBehavior.cs:783-789) and SaveMemory folds only three registered pending kinds (ImmersiveChatBehavior.cs:834-840), so a kinswoman holding an instance loaded before the seal saves straight over it when her reply lands. This is exactly the case the blessing seal — which this code calls its own mold ("the blessing's mold with its sign reversed", Lovers.cs:502-503) — guards against: OnBlessingSealed writes `_pendingBlessingFolds[bride.StringId] = (day, bless.Price, newsBeat);` BEFORE its LoadMemory/SaveMemory, over the comment "the gold can never buy a blessing the world forgets (review find, 2026.08.08)" (Courtship.cs:1471-1480). The neighbouring leak on this same road was fixed the same way on 2026.08.15 (LeakTheBond now uses WriteNightBeat, Lovers.cs:735). Only the ransom was missed — and unlike a beat, LoverRansomPaid is load-bearing state: CanNameHerPrice skips a woman whose house is already paid via `if (LoadMemory(soul).LoverRansomPaid > 0) continue;` (Lovers.cs:100), and WillRideWithYou/BringHerAlong both gate on it (Lovers.cs:588, 626). FAILURE PATH: in the talk screen the player sends a line to his lover Ira (daughter of another house); while her reply is still in flight he switches to her father's thread and seals the price. The gold is paid, Ira's LoverRansomPaid is set and saved; her reply lands a second later and SaveMemory writes her stale instance, so LoverRansomPaid is back to 0 and the beat telling her she was bought is gone. LeaveHerHouse has already moved her to the player's clan, so nothing is refundable — and CanNameHerPrice now offers her father the price a second time, charging the player for her twice.
findings.fix: src/ImmersiveAI.Module/ImmersiveChatBehavior.Lovers.cs, method OnRansomSealed — apply the blessing's own discipline rather than inventing a second shape. Park the paid truth before the direct write and fold it on every save, exactly as `_pendingBlessingFolds`/`FoldPendingBlessing` do (ImmersiveChatBehavior.Courtship.cs:65-88): a `_pendingRansomFolds` dictionary keyed by kin.StringId holding (price, newsBeat); a `FoldPendingRansom(npc, memory)` that fills `memory.LoverRansomPaid` only when it is still 0 and appends the beat only when it is absent (idempotent, the same shape as FoldPendingBlessing); and one more call beside the three in SaveMemory (ImmersiveChatBehavior.cs:836-838). WriteNightBeat alone is not enough here — it would save the beat but not the number, and the number is what the gold bought.

findings.title: HeartBands.Of has no bond parameter — the Core function is right, the Module chooses the reading
findings.evidence: `Of(int relation, CourtshipStage stage)` is a pure function of the two things Core is allowed to know; BondKind lives in the same file but is never a parameter, so the cushion-versus-truth decision is deliberately the Module's — the only layer that can read memory.LoverBond and FamilyBuilder.AreWed. NOTE for the fixer, because it is the root cause of the LoverStandingLine finding and not a defect in itself: the class remark promises more than the signature can deliver — "PAST THE SEAL THERE IS NO CUSHION — betrothal, marriage, the lover's bond: from there what you see is what is there" (HeartBands.cs:78-82) — while a lover's bond is invisible to this function, so every caller must remember to switch to OfRelation by hand. findings.title: MarkFreshWound has no in-flight guard, and its own save EATS the beat LeakTheBond just parked
findings.evidence: MarkFreshWound is still `LoadMemory(her); memory.FreshWoundDay = gameDay; SaveMemory(her, memory);` (Nights.cs:1249-1251) with no IsExchangeInFlight check, and LeakTheBond calls it on the very next line after parking the beat (Lovers.cs:735 then :739). SaveMemory folds via FoldPendingWeddingBeats, which is CONSUMING — `if (!_pendingWeddingBeats.TryRemove(npc.StringId, out var beats) …) return;` (Weddings.cs:69) — so it pulls the just-parked OtherWomanLearnsBeat out of the pending dictionary and writes it into an instance the in-flight turn is about to overwrite (ExecutePlayerTurnAsync holds `memory = ctx.Memory` from L1913 and saves it at L1992). Compare FoldPendingBlessing, which peeks with TryGetValue and is idempotent (Courtship.cs:79). FAILURE: player sends a line to his wife Sibylla in the talk screen (reply in flight, _quickChatBusy holds her), switches to Ira's thread and presses "Take it" on her offer → OnLoverSealed → LeakTheBond parks Sibylla's beat, then MarkFreshWound loads from disk, TryRemoves that beat, folds it in, stamps the wound and writes; Sibylla's reply lands a second later and her stale instance overwrites the file. Beat gone, stamp gone, pending dictionary now empty so FlushParkedWeddingBeats can never recover it, no log line, no notice — she never learned, and the leak → spike → confrontation loop simply does not happen. The comment defending the gap (Lovers.cs:737-738, "A stamp lost to a race costs only a quieter morning, which is why it does not need parking") is untrue as written: it costs the beat too.

Better, and in the existing shape: park the day in a static ConcurrentDictionary<string,double> _pendingWounds and fold it from SaveMemory beside the other three, copying _pendingBlessingFolds' idempotent TryGetValue shape (not TryRemove), plus a sweep alongside FlushParkedWeddingBeats so a talk that simply ends still lands it.

findings.title: LayDutyNightReason writes the spiral raw and eats the parked duty beat the same way (not in the leads)

FAILURE: the wife's reply is still in flight (classic chat window, or the talk screen closed with her answer still coming — _quickChatBusy stays set until it lands); the player clicks the evening's portrait notice and picks "<name> — go to her anyway". result.notes:
SYSTEMIC ROOT behind findings 6, 7 and 8, worth fixing once instead of three times: the mod's invariant is "no SaveMemory on a hero whose exchange is in flight, except from that exchange itself", and the three pending kinds enforce it asymmetrically. FoldPendingWeddingBeats (Weddings.cs:69) and FoldPendingBirthBeats (Births.cs:74) CONSUME with TryRemove; FoldPendingBlessing (Courtship.cs:79) only PEEKS with TryGetValue and is idempotent. Any third-party write that skips the IsExchangeInFlight gate therefore does not merely lose its own data — it silently eats whatever a properly-guarded sibling parked a moment earlier, and FlushParkedWeddingBeats can no longer recover it because the entry is already removed. Alternative one-shot fix to the three local guards: make the two beat folds non-consuming (they already dedupe on `memory.RecentTurns.Any(t => t.PlayerLine == beat)`), leave removal to FlushParkedWeddingBeats, and give that sweep the same dedupe check so it cannot double-append. That closes the class for every future writer as well.

DELIBERATE, DO NOT "FIX": (1) the spike being spent by an UNRELATED outreach (she writes a duty letter that hour and the wound clears) is written into NoteOutreach at NpcMemory.cs:193-196 — "she has gone to him, whatever she chose to say when she got there"; (2) the ponder clearing the stamp on a NO — NoteOutreachConsidered:206-207, "She weighed it and let it pass. That IS her answer to the wound"; (3) nothing writes on her door when a leak lands — argued at Lovers.cs:710-714 and in the design record's item 4; (4) DoorStandingFor deliberately uses the UNCUSHIONED HeartBands.OfRelation for any sealed bond (Doors.cs:93-102, stamped "self-review, 2026.08.15"), which is the already-applied fix for the four duplicate "a lover's door can never go cold" leads — outside my area, but I read the site while tracing the pull machinery and they are ALREADY_FIXED.

KNOWN LIMITATION, reported as such rather than as a defect: a wounded distant soul can be starved of her spike by the post's own gates — MaxLettersInFlight (default 3, Letters.cs:194) returns before the loop, and HasInFlightWith (L215) skips a bond that already has a courier on the road. Both predate the feature, do exactly what their comments say ("the cap, not the moment's socialness, is what protects the later busier self"), and the design record lists "the exact pull-spike shape" as a tuning question for the builder. If Anton wants the confrontation guaranteed, the in-shape answer is to let a wound-driven letter ride outside the cap the way a player-invited reply already does — a design call, not a bug fix.

TRIVIA, unrelated to the leads: ImmersiveChatBehavior.cs:2506-2510 carries two stacked <summary> blocks — the one written for HearthFactor now attaches to HearthWord, which sits between them. Documentation only; likely a CS1571 warning.

result.why: REAL. I could not refute it. `RecordChildsOwnBeginning` (ImmersiveChatBehavior.Births.cs:464) is called from exactly one place — `RecordHourBeats` line 455 — and grep over the whole repo confirms no other caller and no backfill (`OwnBeginningMark`/`ChildBornBeat` appear only in BirthText.cs, RecognitionTests, and that one site). `RecordHourBeats` bails at line 416 unless `BirthAccount` is non-empty and `BirthBeatDone` is false. The fallback branch of `SweepBirthsThatNeverGotTheirBeat` (1271-1292) — reached only when `AnyLived && !BirthBeatDone && BirthAccount blank && BirthAttempts >= BirthLedger.MaxAttempts` (3) — hand-writes `MotherHourBeat` and `FatherBeat`, then sets `record.BirthBeatDone = true` at 1291, which permanently closes `RecordHourBeats` for that record. Nothing repairs it afterwards: `BirthStoryFailed` (1168) only shows one grey notice; `RecordGrief` serves the `!AnyLived` case; `OwnTheChild` (638) writes a different line (`ChildNameBeat`) and only when a name is actually given; `WithholdTheName` writes nothing into the child at all. Reachable under a dead/rate-limited key both ways: while `LlmGate.AutonomyQuiet` is true the sweep is skipped at line 1202, but when the gate reopens the record is already at MaxAttempts, so `BirthLedger.AwaitingHour` (BirthLedger.cs:169) excludes it and the sweep takes it straight down the hand-written branch. Not by design: the sweep's own sibling comment at 1281-1282 ("His mark never depended on the chronicler at all, so losing it here was pure oversight") is the identical argument for the child, BirthText.cs:238-247 says the child's line is hand-written and "costs one hand-written line", and docs/after-the-wedding-design.md item 6 lists `RecordChildsOwnBeginning` + `ChildBornBeat` as "one hand-written line each, no LLM" with no dependency on the account. Not already fixed: the 2026.08.15 self-review comment inside `RecordChildsOwnBeginning` (473-479) touched only the `owned` argument, and the sweep carries no such stamp. The proposed fix is correct and minimal — insert `RecordChildsOwnBeginning(record);` immediately before line 1291. It cannot double-write: the block is reached only when `!record.BirthBeatDone`, and `BirthBeatDone` is set on the next line, which is the same guard the ordinary path uses.
result.correction: Two precisions on the failure story. (1) The claim's "the newborn's memory file stays empty" is exactly right only for a child that is never owned — an unowned child gets nothing from `WithholdTheName`, so its memory holds nothing at all. A child born in marriage, or one whose father later picks a feast or the quiet owning, still receives `ChildNameBeat` from `OwnTheChild` (670), so it would grow up knowing it carries its father's name while never knowing its mother, its birthplace, or the silence it was born into — the `ChildBornBeat` facts are the ones lost in every case. (2) The loss is not confined to a rate-limited key: any three consecutive unusable answers (`LooksLikeAnAccount` false at line 378 — a refusal, a truncation, a malformed reply) reach the same branch, and the sweep also runs the branch for records loaded from a save where the attempts were already spent.

result.item: Let the voices read the *acted* parts, with an MCM toggle on by default
result.rootCause:
THE ITEM IS ALREADY BUILT AND COMMITTED. It landed as `0b03644` "Let the voices read the acted parts, and close a gesture that ends on a word" while I was reading (HEAD is now `b1ff2b0`, working tree clean). Do not build it again. What shipped, verified line by line:

- `src/ImmersiveAI.Module/ModConfig.cs:830` — `public bool VoiceSpeakActedParts { get; set; } = true;` with a full doc block at 818-829. No `Normalize()` clamp (a bool needs none) and no `ConfigVersion` migration — correct: `ModConfig.Load` uses `JsonConvert.DeserializeObject` (ModConfig.cs:1029), so a config.json written before this key keeps the `= true` initializer. "On by default" reaches existing players for free.
- `src/ImmersiveAI.Module/Voice/VoiceService.cs:514-518` inside `PlanFor` — `var acted = Config?.VoiceSpeakActedParts ?? true;` then `SpokenWithGestures` / `SpokenOnly`, read LIVE per line like `AutoCastOn` and `AutoSpeakEnabled`, so the toggle bites on the next line with no restart.
- `src/ImmersiveAI.Core/Voices/SpeakableText.cs:55-71` — `SpokenWithGestures` now runs every segment through a new private `Closed()` that appends a full stop when a segment ends on a letter or digit.
- MCM: `ImmersiveAiMcmSettings.cs:233-236` ("Read the acted parts aloud too", group "Voices" GroupOrder=3, Order=5, `RequireRestart=false`, hint 281 chars — inside the ~320 budget); `McmBridge.cs:253` MenuSignature, `:287` CfgSignature, `:357` PushConfigToMenu, `:467` PullMenuToConfig. `RepairMenuInstance` needs nothing (it only rebuilds null Dropdowns), `McmChoiceLists` needs nothing (no list), `TryRescueOnce` needs nothing (it rescues keys/models/endpoints/backend only, and a stored bool cannot be told from its default). Wiring is complete and correct.
- CHANGELOG.md:51 has its pill under "### Hearing them speak".

ON THE NAMED TRAP — SAY IT PLAINLY: **the cache key already covers the flip, and `VoiceCacheKey` needs no change at all.** `VoiceService.cs:524` hashes `spoken` — the exact string handed to both engines (hosted: `CloudVoiceClient.SynthesizeAsync(config, plan.SpeakerName, plan.Text, path)` at :974; local Streaming/FullRead: `text: plan.Text` at :1089; ByLine: `plan.Bites` at :1029, chunks of the same string). Flip the toggle and a gesture-bearing reply produces a different string, hence a different 64-bit key, hence a different `_cache\<voiceId>\<key>\` folder. A reply with no gesture produces the same string and correctly hits the same audio. `VoiceCacheKey.For` is called in exactly ONE production place (`VoiceService.cs:524`), so there is nowhere else for this to go wrong. It is free — and it is *unpinned by any test*, which is gap #2 below.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT, and it is real:

1. **`Closed()` fixes one end of the seam and opens the other.** SpeakableText.cs:65-71 gives the gesture an ending but never lifts its first letter — and `IsContinuation` (SpeakableText.cs:223-234) reads *a lone stop followed by a lower-case letter as an abbreviation and refuses to cut there*. Gestures are overwhelmingly written lower-case (`*sets down her cup*`, `*she rises*` — the tests' own examples). So "…since the fords. she sets down the cup." loses **the fords' own sentence end**: `Chunk` merges the sentence before the gesture into the same bite, which is precisely the "nowhere to breathe" the commit set out to fix, and the engine reads the join with continuation prosody rather than as a new sentence.
2. **The trap has no test.** `VoiceCacheKeyTests.cs:105-116` pins the opposite half (with gestures dropped, editing a gesture must NOT invalidate audio). Nothing pins "flipping the toggle must not replay the other setting's clip" — the guarantee lives only in a comment at VoiceService.cs:511-513.
3. **`PlanFor` derives the same string twice, by two different entry points** (`:515` `SpokenWithGestures(text)` for the key and the engine, `:518` `BitesFor(text, includeGestures: acted)` for the bites). They agree today only because both read the same `acted` local — and the whole no-stale-audio guarantee rests on them agreeing. Also parses the body through `EmoteText` twice per line.
4. **`IsWorthSpeaking` (SpeakableText.cs:74) still answers from `SpokenOnly` alone.** No Module caller today (grep: tests only), so no live bug — but it now answers `false` for a gesture-only reply that the DEFAULT settings will happily speak. A trap for the next caller.
5. **Doc drift at three sites, all now stating the opposite of the default:** SpeakableText.cs:13-16 ("gestures are acted, not spoken … a voice reading that aloud is instantly a robot reading stage directions") states as law what is now a setting; TalkScreenVM.cs:609-611 ("the gestures are acted, not read aloud (SpeakableText strips them)"); CLAUDE.md:1772-1775, whose config list has no `VoiceSpeakActedParts` — and whose `VoiceSpeakReachOuts` parenthetical still says "(off …)" when ModConfig.cs:908 has been `= true` since 2026.08.15.

plan.change: Lift a gesture's first letter, not just close its tail. Add a private `AsNarration` beside `Closed` (after line 71) and, at line 59, route GESTURE segments through it while speech segments keep plain `Closed`. Capitalize only when the first char is a lower-case letter, so a gesture opening on a digit or a dash is untouched. This string is never seen by a player — the thread draws `*seg.Text*` straight from `EmoteText` (TalkScreenVM.cs:627) — it goes only to the engine and to the cache manifest, which is why lifting a letter is not the same kind of act as adding a stop.

Line 74: add an overload that knows about the setting, keeping the one-argument form delegating to `false` so the existing test and its meaning stand. Nothing in the Module calls this today; the point is that the next caller must not be told a gesture-only reply is unspeakable while the default speaks it.

Line 518: chunk the string that was already built, instead of parsing the body a second time. Identical output today (`BitesFor` is literally `Chunk(SpokenOnly|SpokenWithGestures)`), half the `EmoteText` work per line, and — the real reason — it makes it structurally impossible for the text that is HASHED and the text that is CHUNKED to drift apart. Extend the comment at :511-513 to say that is now guaranteed by shape rather than by discipline.

Lines 13-16: the file's own opening still states as law the thing that is now a setting, and states it the wrong way round — the default reads them aloud. Reword the first job: gestures are told APART from the words, and whether they are then read as narration is `VoiceSpeakActedParts` (on by default); off, they are dropped, because a voice reciting stage directions is a robot. Keep the second job (chunking) exactly as it is.

Lines 609-611: "the gestures are acted, not read aloud (SpeakableText strips them)" is now conditional and false by default. The conclusion is unchanged and worth keeping — ONE mark for the whole message rather than one per fragment — so only the reason needs mending: the ▶ speaks the whole message, acted parts included or not as the player has set it, which is another reason a single mark is the truth of it.

plan.symbol: three existing expectations the capital moves
plan.change: The capital changes three shipped assertions and they must move with it, or the suite goes red. Line 44: `"she looks up, slowly. Well?"` → `"She looks up, slowly. Well?"`. Line 52: `"she laughs! Well?"` → `"She laughs! Well?"` (and add to its comment that the CAPITAL is not the same kind of act as a second stop — it is for the chunker and the engine, and never reaches the page). Line 70: `Assert.Contains("turns away", with[0])` breaks on case — the text is now "Turns away without a word." — so assert `"Turns away"`.

Three additions. (1) The mechanism test — the sentence BEFORE a lower-case gesture must still end; assert on the first bite, which is the discriminating one (without the capital it reads "…fords. she sets down the cup."). (2) Cyrillic, because the mod is played in Bulgarian and `char.ToUpperInvariant` over Cyrillic is the sort of thing that gets assumed. (3) The all-gesture reply is worth speaking when the acted parts are read.

Pin THE TRAP. Nothing was added to the key for the toggle — the property falls out of the key being built from the text actually handed to the engine — so a test is the only thing that will notice if a later 'optimization' keys on `SpokenOnly` while sending the acted text. Both halves: different key when there IS an acted part, same key when there is not (else every ordinary line would be made twice on a flip). Give the plain body an ordinary ending; `Closed()` deliberately completes an unpunctuated last word, so a body ending mid-word legitimately keys differently.

Two mends in one touch. Add `VoiceSpeakActedParts` to the list with the three facts worth carrying forward (the asterisks never reach the engine because EmoteText hands back the CONTENT; a gesture is closed AND lifted or the sentence before it loses its cut point in `IsContinuation`; the cache needed nothing because the key is built from the spoken text). And correct the stale parenthetical on `VoiceSpeakReachOuts`, which still says "(off …)" though ModConfig.cs:908 has been `= true` since 2026.08.15.
